newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan king urges Clinton to act on Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan king urges Clinton to act on Mideast.

text.p: King Hassan of Morocco on Wednesday congratulated U.S. President Bill Clinton on his re-election and urged him to devote himself to the Middle East peace process and respect of previous commitments.
Describing the path to a just Middle East peace and mutual recognition, notably between Palestinians and Israelis, as "long and precarious", King Hassan told Clinton:
"Your determination and personal convictions, with no doubt, will make prevail reason and respect for commitments already taken."

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been accused by the Palestinians of reneging on agreements reached between President Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority and the previous Israeli government, ousted in elections earlier this year.
U.S.-sponsored Israeli-PLO talks are deadlocked over the implementation of the Israeli troop pullback in Hebron, home to 400 Jewish settlers and 100,000 Palestinians.
Palestinians accuse Israel of trying to renegotiate the Hebron deal under which Israel was due to redeploy in Hebron last March.
The pullback was put on hold after suicide bombings that killed 59 people in Israel in February and March. Netanyahu says he wants to boost security for Jews in Hebron.
